title: The 10 Best Stephen Wilson Jr. Songs Every New Fan Should Hear - NewsBreak
text:
By Carena Liptak ,
9 hours ago Michael Hickey, Getty Images When the nominations for the 2025 CMA Awards came out, it was many mainstream country fans’ first introduction to Stephen Wilson Jr., who scored a New Artist of the Year nod.
But there’s more to Wilson Jr. than meets the eye — and not just because, at 46, he’s significantly older than the average contender in the category.
Wilson Jr. formed the indie rock group AutoVaughn during his senior year of college and spent about five years touring with the band.
After leaving the group, he stepped away from music entirely, pursuing a research and development career in a food science lab. Despite the sharp left turn — a move that provided financial security to raise his stepson — he never let go of his passion for songwriting.
He signed a publishing deal in 2016 and started releasing indie rock-flavored country singles in the late 2010s, as well as writing songs for artists like Dierks Bentley and Lori McKenna .
Much of the music Wilson was writing was inspired by his father’s death in 2018, following emergency surgery.
In processing that loss, he also began to write about his upbringing with a single father, while his mother was often absent and involved in abusive relationships.
The result was Søn of Dad , an album that explores grief, loss, and shifting identity.
Read More : 30 Country Songs About Death
The project came out in 2023, on the five-year anniversary of Wilson’s father’s death. It earned him a powerful grassroots fan base and cemented his status as an artist to watch in the Americana and indie country scenes.
Now, as he looks ahead toward the CMA Awards and beyond, Wilson is making his move into mainstream stardom.
Keep reading for Taste of Country’s primer on the essential Stephen Wilson Jr. songs every new fan should hear.
The 10 Best Stephen Wilson Jr. Songs Every New Fan Should Hear Stephen Wilson Jr. first emerged onto many mainstream country fans' radars when he scored a CMA New Artist of the Year nomination in 2025, but there's more to this country newcomer than meets the eye. He's written songs for artists such as Dierks Bentley and Lori McKenna and, at 46 years old, is quite a bit more seasoned than your typical fresh-faced country music upstart. Keep reading for Taste of Country's primer on Stephen Wilson Jr.'s music Gallery Credit: Carena Liptak Frazer Harrison, Getty Images "I'm a Song" Wilson has said that “I’m a Song” was his late father’s favorite among his own tracks—and, in fact, that his father considered it his favorite song of all time.
The lyrics offer a tender appreciation of music and the emotional power it holds over people’s lives. Michael Hickey, Getty Images "Kid" Wilson was raised by a single father while his mother was often absent and the tougher parts of his childhood play into his songwriting on the music of his Søn of Dad album.
In "Kid," Wilson speaks from the perspective of looking at a child's life from the outside in. " Sorry life's so hard, kid ," he sings toward the end of the track. Kate Green "The Devil" This haunting track from Wilson’s Søn of Dad album takes a sweeping look at pain and hardship: opioid addiction, school shootings, and sexual abuse all surface in its wide-ranging lyrics.
“ There’s the one you know, there’s the one you don’t / But they’re still both the devil ,” Wilson sings in the chorus.
Kate Green, Getty Images "Father's Søn" This song is a gritty and personal ode to the dad who raised Wilson and gave him his name. He also recorded a duet version with Hardy . Jason Kempin, Getty Images "Took a Walk" (with Shaboozey) Wilson contributed “Took a Walk” to the soundtrack of the film The Long Walk .
A collaboration with Shaboozey , the track pairs their voices perfectly on this evocative ballad. Jason Kempin, Getty Images "American Gothic" (with Hailey Whitters) This track stands out in Wilson’s discography as a rare male–female duet and one of the more anthemic, upbeat songs in his catalog. Hailey Whitters brings vocal power and a touch of nostalgia to this groovy country rocker.
Mike Coppola, Getty Images "Grief is Only Love" Wilson's vocals shine on this vulnerable ballad, which visits familiar themes of grief and loss. . At moments, his voice is so evocative that you might mistake it for Chris Stapleton ’s on first listen.
Frazer Harrison, Getty Images "Stand By Me" (Ben E. King Cover) "Stand By Me" is a perfect cover choice for Wilson, whose voice delivers a powerful emotional punch. In this fan-favorite version, he puts his own gritty spin on a classic. Jeff Schear, Getty Images "Cuckoo" Wilson lets his inner rocker out in "Cuckoo," a hard-driving song that rails against the everyday oppression of being a working-class American. Kate Green, Getty Images "Year to Be Young 1994" This track offers a grungy take on nostalgia and growing up in the ’90s, packed with cultural references that ’90s kids are sure to appreciate.
